must_fix.claim: A verifier trained on D2 alone reaches AUROC=1.000 on held-out V10 (and the symmetric V10->D2), presented as a property of the Phase G verifier / as same-rig cross-session generalization of the headline result.
must_fix.problem: Scope-blurring / model conflation. The cross-session AUROC=1.000 results come ONLY from the Stage-0 cross-verifiers trained to 100k steps (experiments/stage_0_cross_verifier/{d2_only,v10_only}_verifier/step_00100000/summary.json — confirmed the ONLY subdir is step_00100000). The canonical Phase G 'main' verifier is a DIFFERENT model: 25k steps, 39.77M params, and its only evals (main/shuffled/synthetic_positive) are WITHIN-session, explicitly caveated 'within-session generalization, NOT cross-session' (diagnostic_report.md L77). The paper attributes the cross-session result to 'the verifier' without disclosing it is a separate 100k-step Stage-0 model with a different training regime and a fake/real eval schema. impl_truth.json trust_flag (L97, L391) flags exactly this conflation.
must_fix.fix: Explicitly attribute every cross-session AUROC=1.000 to the Stage-0 100k-step leave-one-session-out verifiers, NOT the 25k Phase G main run. State that the canonical Phase G headline (AUROC=1.000) is within-session only, and that cross-session is a separate experiment with separate models. Cite stage_0_cross_verifier/.../step_00100000/summary.json for the cross-session claim and main/eval/summary.json for the within-session headline.

must_fix.claim: The verifier operates across both v9 and v10, giving a same-rig CROSS-PROTOCOL generalization result.

No experiment trains on one protocol and tests held-out on the other as an independent variable.
must_fix.fix: Replace 'cross-protocol generalization' with 'the verifier was trained and evaluated within-session across both chain protocols (v9 on D2, v10 on V10)'. Do not frame protocol-mixing during training as a generalization result.

paper_vs_video: DENOISING FRAMING: The video (and impl_truth safe-to-claim) frames Phase G as a DENOISER — 'a genuine pair denoises cleanly = low residual.' The paper's abstract/intro says 'The verifier does NOT denoise; it reports the noise-prediction residual.' Both are defensible but the wording collides. impl_truth.json denoiser_resolution L515 explicitly says 'DO NOT say it never denoises the fake — keep the denoising framing.' The paper should align: it is an epsilon-prediction (denoising-diffusion) net used as a scoring function — it computes a noise-prediction residual at fixed timesteps and does not run the full reverse sampling loop. Avoid the bare phrase 'does not denoise', which contradicts the video's denoiser framing.

overall.recommendation: REVISE BEFORE PUBLICATION — not publishable as-is, but no evidence of fabricated core results. The headline within-session results (AUROC=1.000 correct-vs-wrong on D2 n=198 / V10 n=200, delta_wrong +0.0040/+0.0041, shuffled control 0.5006 / 7e-8, synthetic-positive 1.000, F-A v1 caught at AUROC=1.000 across all 4 checkpoints, 39.77M params, ControlNet-not-FiLM-on-E, 8-bit end-to-end, frame counts) are ALL verified directly against eval-output JSON and code — this part is solid and well-controlled. Two genuine CONTRADICTIONS must be fixed: (1) Sec 3.2 'no warm-up' vs code warmup=500 (and the paper self-contradicts Sec 09); (2) the cross-session AUROC=1.000 is silently attributed to 'the verifier' when it is a separate 100k-step Stage-0 model, not the canonical 25k Phase G run — this scope-blur is the single most serious issue and recurs in 01/02/03/11. Several BLOCKER-severity claims rest on eval outputs absent from the local mirror: the Mask R-CNN body/off-body segmentation table (E2_seg 0.009-0.538, E3_seg 1.000 — appears only in SESSION_HANDOFF prose; the proper_segmentation directory does not exist on disk), the 35/53-condition extended XOF-perturbation sweep (item_1 summary.json contains only correct/wrong/uncond/lag — no Type 1-6/octave/swap results), and EXP 6 n=120 ranking. These are likely real outputs that live on Lambda and were excluded from the mirror, but as written the paper cites numbers with no locatable backing and partly against the DO-NOT-CLAIM list. Note one FALSE-ALARM in the upstream per-section pass: the checkpoint-size 'CONTRADICTION' (456 vs 478 MB) is a MiB/MB confusion — the paper's 477,531,127 bytes is exactly correct. Action: fix the two contradictions, disambiguate every cross-session/cross-protocol attribution to the Stage-0 verifiers, and either attach the Lambda eval outputs for the segmentation/perturbation/EXP-6 tables or soften those claims. After that, the paper is publishable within its stated same-rig two-session scope.
